claims.claim: the Sahara has been gaining vegetation along its edges in recent decades
claims.definition: increase in greenness (NDVI) measured by satellites across the Sahel and parts of the Sahara fringe, particularly since the 1980s
claims.measured_value: trend (NDVI + satellite vegetation indices; +11% NDVI across the Sahel per multiple studies)
claims.authoritative_source: multiple peer-reviewed satellite-based analyses (e.g. Anyamba & Tucker; Brandt et al.; Zeng & Bristow)
claims.notes: the trend is well documented; the magnitude varies by study and region

claims.claim: the Sahara covers roughly nine point two million square kilometers
claims.definition: commonly cited area for the Sahara desert, about 9.2 million km2

claims.claim: satellite data since the 1980s shows vegetation increasing across the Sahel
claims.definition: NDVI and related vegetation indices from AVHRR (since 1981) and MODIS (since 2000) show a positive trend in Sahel greenness
claims.measured_value: trend direction +~11% in NDVI over the Sahel across the 1980s-2010s
claims.authoritative_source: Anyamba & Tucker 2005; Brandt et al. 2015; e.g. Zeng & Bristow 2015

claims.claim: the greening is linked to a recovery of Sahel rainfall after the 1970s-1980s droughts and to CO2 fertilization
claims.definition: the post-1980s Sahel rainfall recovery (interdecadal variability) and elevated atmospheric CO2 (which reduces stomatal water loss) both contribute to increased vegetation
claims.authoritative_source: IPCC AR6 (Africa chapter); peer-reviewed attribution studies
claims.notes: qualitative wording ('linked to') to match the attribution certainty

claims.claim: the deep Sahara core remains largely unchanged; the greening is limited to the Sahel rim
claims.definition: the high-temperature, very-low-rainfall core of the Sahara does not show significant vegetation trend; the green gains are spatially restricted to the Sahel and margins
claims.measured_value: spatial pattern (Sahel-vs-core difference in NDVI trends)
claims.authoritative_source: Brandt et al. 2015; other remote-sensing syntheses
